activity_context.topic_title: Solving Decoupled Homogeneous Systems of ODEs

feedback.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)})}^{-2t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{2}^{-2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(1)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{6} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=1$ into the general solution, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(1) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {2}^{-2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{6} \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}{e}^{5} \\ \frac{{c}_{2}}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}e \\ 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =e[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+4[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{2}^{-2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}e \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]{2}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$
